  "text": "On the hill above Bellweather stood a clock tower that had been silent for nearly thirty years. Its hands were fixed at 4:17, and pigeons nested beneath its cracked stone ledges. Most people hurried past without looking up.

Nina noticed the tower because she was waiting for the bus after school. One windy afternoon, she heard a faint ticking from somewhere inside. The next day, she returned with a flashlight and found a narrow door hidden behind ivy. It opened onto a spiral staircase, dusty but sturdy.

At the top, Nina discovered gears, springs, and a workbench covered in tools. A note lay beneath a brass key: “If you can hear the clock, it is ready to wake.”

She showed the note to Mr. Vale, the retired watchmaker who lived near the square. He studied the key and told her the tower’s bell had stopped when its winding chain broke. Together, they climbed the stairs, carrying a new length of chain and a toolbox.

The repair took all afternoon. Nina held the lantern while Mr. Vale fitted the links, and they worked carefully around the great iron gears. Just before sunset, he nodded for her to pull the lever.

The clock shuddered. Its hands crept forward, then began to move. A deep, clear chime rolled over the rooftops, startling pigeons into flight and drawing people from shops and doorways.

From then on, Nina visited every week to help Mr. Vale keep the clock running. And whenever the bell sounded, the town paused for a moment—not to check the time, but to remember that even quiet things could begin again."
